ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under FINTRAC rules (PCMLTFA ss. 11.1-11.2 and SOR/2002-184 ss. 52-53): (i) positively identify the corporate client and every individual with significant control at the 25% threshold; (ii) screen all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the OSFI Consolidated Sanctions List, Global Affairs Canada Part 1 (UN) and Part 2 (domestic) sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list (applicable for USD wire clearing), UN Consolidated List, and HM Treasury consolidated list for correspondent banking; (iii) assess domestic and foreign politically exposed persons status (heads of state, ministers, senators, senior judges, senior public officials, and their family members and close associates) and apply enhanced due diligence with senior management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring where any PEP flag appears; (iv) maintain seven-year record retention and file to FINTRAC any Cash Transaction Report (CAD 10,000 or more), Suspicious Transaction Report under s. 7 PCMLTFA, and Electronic Funds Transfer Report; (v) confirm the Low_Risk_Standard classification for this creative game-art outsourcing BPO (NAICS 541430) with Wire Transfer and PayPal payment rails, absent sanctions or PEP flags.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (BC Registry Services, Registry of Joint Stock Companies, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia) — corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: BC BCA s. 28 and BC Corporate Registry Name Guidelines: the statutory corporate name must be in Latin script (English or French); a Chinese or non-Roman script name cannot be registered as the legal name and may be used only as an unofficial translated style. A BC ULC must include the legal element Unlimited Liability Company, the abbreviation ULC, or the French equivalent Societe a responsabilite illimitee. Each name must be distinguishable from all existing BC, federal, and relevant extra-provincial registers, and consist of a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and the legal element; numerals and ampersands are restricted unless part of a distinctive combination.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government affiliation tokens: ROYAL, CROWN, GOVERNMENT, MUNICIPAL, FEDERAL, PROVINCIAL, MINISTERIAL — require prior written consent of the appropriate minister

Regulated profession and trade tokens: LAWYER, ATTORNEY, BARRISTER, NOTARY, BANK, TRUST, INSURANCE, ENGINEER, ARCHITECT, ACCOUNTANT, AUDITOR, COLLEGE, INSTITUTE, UNIVERSITY, CHAMBER OF COMMERCE, BOARD OF TRADE — require consent or reservation by the applicable regulatory body
Obscene, scandalous, or immoral expressions (BC BCA s. 28(1)(a))
CANADA or BRITISH COLUMBIA within the name require prior authorization (BC BCA s. 28(2)(b))
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, BC Registry issues a refusal notice through Corporate Online. The applicant may, within 30 days of refusal, file a written request for administrative reconsideration with the Director of Corporate Registration in Victoria, including legal and factual submissions, supporting consents (e.g., regulator consent letters), and evidence of distinctiveness; the Registrar re-evaluates the name against the BC BCA, distinguishability requirements, Name Guidelines, and the public interest. If administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may (i) file a fresh Name Request (CAD 30 fee) listing up to three alternative names in order of preference, (ii) commence a judicial review application in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under BC BCA s. 25 seeking an order directing the Registrar to reserve or accept the name, or (iii) incorporate under an approved alternative name and concurrently file a post-incorporation Name Change.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. BC BCA s. 36 requires a registered office at an actual street address in British Columbia (a post office box is prohibited) attended during business hours; a licensed virtual office providing a physical BC street address, mail handling, and telephone answering satisfies the statutory requirement for this industry (creative game-art outsourcing, no statutory license, no public-facing premises). The registered records office, where the central securities register, register of directors, and register of individuals with significant control are physically kept, must also be in British Columbia and may coincide with the registered office. A virtual office alone is adequate for a non-operational or holding ULC; however, once the ULC employs local 3D artists or operates a Canadian studio, a physical lease becomes commercially necessary for employer compliance, CRA commercial-substance, and nexus reasons.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified at approximately 5% annual probability for a newly incorporated low-risk services ULC. BC Registry does not conduct routine unannounced registered-office site inspections; FINTRAC examinations are weighted toward money services businesses and high-risk sectors, whereas this file is classified Low_Risk_Standard with Wire Transfer and PayPal rails; the Canada Revenue Agency year-one books-and-records audit probability is below 2% absent large losses or anomalous fund movements. Unannounced inspections would realistically be triggered only by a Suspicious Transaction Report, a tax audit flag, or a land-transparency filing under the Land Owner Transparency Act, none of which is expected in this scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: British Columbia Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, as amended, including the incorporation provisions, unlimited liability company designation rules, Notice of Articles requirements, and registered office provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Mobile Services (BC Corporate Online).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Articles of Incorporation filed electronically through the BC Corporate Online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the BC Business Corporations Act, and no escrow account is mandated. The unlimited liability company may be incorporated with nil issued capital, and shares may be subscribed for nominal or such consideration as the first board approves. Any paid-up capital must be supported by written subscription records in the corporate records office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, this 1st day of [Month, Year], by the sole director as the first board of CA__CA_BC__CA_ULC__ISIC_7490_03_GAME_3D_ART_OUTSOURCING, that: 1. The subscription for 100 common shares of the unlimited liability company by the founding shareholder is accepted and the shares are declared issued upon receipt of aggregate consideration of CAD 0.01. 2. The registered office is fixed at [physical/street address], British Columbia, and [Name of Registered Office Contact] is appointed as the company's registered office contact. 3. [Name of Officer 1], [Name of Officer 2] and [Name of Officer 3] are appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, respectively, to hold office until the next annual general meeting. 4. The directors and officers are authorized to open bank accounts, issue share certificates and execute all incorporation completion documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Mobile Services – BC Corporate Online Name Request Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request through BC Corporate Online. The system performs a NUANS-style registry search against existing BC corporate names. Provide a first-choice name and at least two alternate names. The proposed name must comply with BC unlimited liability company naming rules, including use of 'ULC' or an approved equivalent. Pay the required name-request fee. A successful name reservation is valid for 56 calendar days. No notarization is required for the name request.
required_dossiers: Completed BC Corporate Online name request application
NUANS or BC registry name search report
First-choice name and two alternate corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or objected to as confusingly similar, submit rebuttal evidence, obtain written consent from the conflicting name holder, or select one of the alternate names. If the reserved name expires, file a fresh name request for the same or amended proposed name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Notice of Articles and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal agent; no prior registry approval required for drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Notice of Articles and Articles for the BC unlimited liability company. The Notice of Articles must include the ULC designation, authorized share structure, first directors, registered office address, and any restrictions on the company's business. The Articles may address voting rights, share transfer restrictions, director indemnity, and special rights attaching to each class of shares. The incorporator must sign the dated incorporation application and the directors must sign consents to act. Notarization is generally not required for standard BC filings, but signatures should be witnessed where local counsel advises.
required_dossiers: Notice of Articles draft
Articles draft
Consent to act as director for each proposed first director
Registered office address and consent of occupant
Signed incorporation application and declaration of incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BC registry queries an ambiguous provision, amend the Notice of Articles or Articles and re-file the corrected document on the same BC Corporate Online account. Refusal of a name reservation does not prevent re-filing with a different name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Mobile Services – BC Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the final Notice of Articles and Articles together with the incorporation application through BC Corporate Online. Pay the statutory filing fee of CAD 350.00 (approximate USD 257.00; the registry accepts Canadian currency). Upon successful processing, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Notice of Articles becomes the public constitutional document. Record the company number and incorporation date in the corporate minute book and retain the certified Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Final Notice of Articles
Final Articles
Director consents to act
Registered office address confirmation
Valid payment instrument for the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or placed on hold, the Registrar issues a non-compliance or correction notice. Cure by filing the corrected record through BC Corporate Online within the period specified in the notice or by paying any prescribed correction fee. Substantive legal objections should be resolved by amending the Articles and re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Records Office Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / corporate statutory agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain a registered office physically located in British Columbia at the address stated in the Notice of Articles. The office must be accessible for service of process during ordinary business hours, unless a records-only office arrangement is elected and permitted under the Act. If the registered office changes after incorporation, file the prescribed Notice of Change of Registered Office through BC Corporate Online. Establish the corporate records office to hold the minute book, securities register, director register, officer register, and accounting books.
required_dossiers: Registered office physical address in British Columbia
Consent of the registered office owner or occupant
Records office address and hours of access
Corporate minute book or corporate records binder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If service at the registered office is ineffective or the registry objects to the address, promptly file a Notice of Change of Registered Office with a valid new BC address and fresh occupant consent. Continued non-compliance may trigger default actions by the Registrar requiring a compliance filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors / sole director of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or obtain the signed written consent resolution of all directors. Adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, which must approve the share subscription and issuance, fix the registered office, appoint the chief executive officer, chief financial officer and corporate secretary, and authorize the opening of bank accounts and execution of banking mandates. Record the resolution in the corporate minute book, issue share certificates to the founding shareholder, and file any director or officer changes in the corporate records if required.
required_dossiers: Written consent resolution or minutes of the first board meeting
Pro-forma first board resolution
Share subscription agreements and evidence of consideration
Officer appointment letters and contact information
Bank account authorization and signatory forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the initial board or officer appointments are later found invalid, obtain a subsequent written consent resolution of the incorporator and directors ratifying all pre-incorporation contracts and organizational acts, and correct the officer records in the corporate records office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing board is engaged for ISIC 7490 creative game art outsourcing. Premises-level licensing: City of Vancouver Licensing Department or applicable host municipality. Occupational safety: WorkSafeBC.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: City of Vancouver Business Licence and Building Occupancy Permit. No sector-specific statutory industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required for a 3D art outsourcing studio.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy / Environmental Assessment Office; federal Environment and Climate Change Canada.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. A digital 3D art outsourcing office is not a reviewable project under the British Columbia Environmental Assessment Act or the Canadian Environmental Assessment Act, and no EIA certificate is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater discharges must comply with Metro Vancouver Sewer Use Bylaw limits if connected to municipal sanitary sewerage. HVAC refrigerants must meet the Ozone-Depleting Substances and Halocarbon Alternatives Regulations (SOR/2016-137). No process VOCs are expected from digital-only art production. E-waste and obsolete computer hardware must be managed under the BC Recycling Regulation and applicable electronic waste protocols.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required before occupation, including fire code occupancy approval, tested fire alarms and extinguishers, unobstructed egress, and posted emergency evacuation procedures. A structural load inspection is required if server racks, workstations, or storage areas approach floor-loading limits. WorkSafeBC registration and occupational health and safety clearance are mandatory for the studio workplace, including use of safe materials for 3D printing or traditional sculpting ancillary processes and WHMIS compliance where applicable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility for current account transactions including trade remittances and profit distributions. Capital account transactions require prior Bank of Canada approval for certain investments exceeding CAD 100 million or are subject to reporting thresholds. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted post-corporate tax clearance and subject to 25% dividend withholding tax with FINTRAC reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Act, Canadian corporations must repatriate export proceeds within 90 days of receipt and surrender them to authorized foreign exchange dealers at the market rate on the surrender date. Non-compliance may attract administrative penalties and reporting obligations to FINTRAC.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: PayPal and similar fintech electronic money issuers are viable for inbound client payments with volume limits and mandatory FINTRAC registration. Offshore digital EMIs face legal constraints under Canadian AML regulations including enhanced due diligence for cross-border transfers and potential account restrictions for high-volume game asset transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier 1 domestic commercial banks require directors and authorized signers to appear physically for corporate account opening and KYC interviews. Remote digital onboarding is permitted for lower-value accounts via verified digital identity platforms but mandates in-person verification for accounts exceeding CAD 250,000 or involving non-resident ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership disclosure gaps or high-risk client jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate minute books, shareholder agreements, beneficial ownership certificates, payment contracts, and source-of-funds documentation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment patterns or volume spikes from gaming clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service agreements, delivery confirmations, IP assignment records, and FINTRAC-compliant transaction summaries

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wires with purpose code 900 for equity contributions. Verification requires board resolutions, shareholder agreements, and proof of source of funds. All transfers undergo AML screening and FINTRAC FX reporting within prescribed timelines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements cleared via SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600. Settlements require valid invoices, proof of service delivery, and compliance with Canadian export controls where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts for currency exposure hedging
Non-Deliverable Forwards for emerging market currencies
Currency swaps for long-term liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (company registry annual filing under Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of incorporation, every calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 60; certificate of compliance is withheld; two consecutive unfiled annual reports expose the company to administrative strike-off by the registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including BC provincial corporate allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and BC Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; interest under section 161 of the Income Tax Act; no strike-off consequence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private BC ULC must appoint an auditor unless all shareholders unanimously waive the appointment. Mandatory audit is not triggered primarily by asset or revenue thresholds; a reporting issuer under the BC Securities Act, a public corporation, a bank, a trust and a loan or insurance business are subject to compulsory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Canada (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for reporting issuers; a non-reporting private BC ULC may use Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BC ULC must maintain an individuals with significant control register. Each annual report cycle requires a statement confirming the ISC register is current. Changes in significant control must be filed with the registrar within 14 days via an ISC change notice, and share transfer entries must record date, consideration, and resulting member identity.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Copy of Articles, Notice of Articles, and resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300-800 per year for registered office and registered agent services in British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-18,000 for an external audit of a small private ULC; a US GAAP bridge or parent-required reporting package may add USD 3,000-8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED tax credits (federal 35% refundable for CCPCs, 15% non-refundable for others); BC Digital Media Tax Credit (17.5% refundable for eligible interactive digital media products)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically via CRA My Business Account or approved tax software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a ULC with non-resident shareholders, the corporation is a Canadian resident and files as a Canadian corporation; non-resident shareholders do not file T2.
Compute federal tax on taxable income; no special non-resident treatment.
Compute BC provincial tax; no special non-resident treatment.
Sum of federal and provincial taxes.
Claim applicable credits; non-resident shareholders are not eligible for these credits.
Indicates final amount payable or refundable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on late payments at prescribed rates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide a Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Treaty Benefits) and a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their tax authority. The withholding agent (the ULC) must retain these documents and reduce the withholding rate accordingly.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate 25% for royalties and interest; treaty rates may reduce (e.g., US treaty: royalties 0% for certain IP, 10% for others; interest 0% for arm's length, 15% otherwise).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 50,000,000 gross revenue (for mandatory Master File and Local File); also T106 filing required for transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000 (goods) or CAD 500,000 (services)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have explicit ESR, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and substance-over-form principles apply. For treaty benefits, the Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clause may require economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully evading tax by underreporting income, overstating deductions, or failing to remit withholdings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% of tax evaded plus interest; criminal prosecution with fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they failed to withhold and remit, or if they participated in the evasion scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a ULC as a shell to avoid tax without economic substance, such as artificial intercompany transactions or treaty shopping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can reassess and impose penalties under GAAR; potential denial of treaty benefits and additional taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly participated in the scheme or failed to ensure compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to comply with AML/KYC requirements under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, such as inadequate client due diligence or reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to CAD 500,000 for first offense; criminal penalties for non-compliance, including fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for fines if they failed to implement adequate AML policies or knowingly allowed non-compliance.
